deep.reconstruction:
Context: Euler is treating steady outflow of water through a tube of variable cross-section zz, with arc length s and vertical depth x below the top AB. He assumes, as in §11 of the memoir, that friction gives a retarding force αp/z, i.e. proportional to the local pressure p (Coulomb-style, as for solids) and inversely to the tube's linear size. The term 4b^4 v dz/z^5 is the inertial (velocity-head) term from continuity, with section velocity proportional to 1/zz and head v standing for the efflux head. The momentum balance (§21–22) is the linear first-order ODE dp + α p ds/z = dx + 4b^4 v dz/z^5. With r = ∫ds/z, the integrating factor is e^{αr}, which gives e^{αr}p = C + ∫e^{αr}dx + 4b^4 v∫e^{αr}dz/z^5.

On this page Euler integrates both quadratures by parts using dr = ds/z:
(i) ∫e^{αr}dx = e^{αr}x − α∫e^{αr} x ds/z;
(ii) ∫e^{αr}dz/z^5 = −e^{αr}/(4z^4) + (α/4)∫e^{αr} ds/z^5.
This yields the closed form p = Ce^{−αr} + x − αe^{−αr}∫e^{αr}x ds/z − b^4v/z^4 + αb^4 v e^{−αr}∫e^{αr}ds/z^5.

Because α is very small, he then expands e^{±αr} and collects powers of α up to α^3. The result is a perturbation series in the friction coefficient: the frictionless Bernoulli-type pressure C + x − b^4v/z^4, plus corrections at O(α), O(α^2) and O(α^3).

§25 sets up a test case (Tab. VI, Fig. 3). A vertical cylindrical vessel ABEF has area gg and height a and is kept full. It is joined to an inclined cylindrical tube FCD of length b and area ff, making angle ζ with the vertical, which ends in an orifice CD of area hh.

§26 begins with the upper vessel, where z = g, ds = dx and r = x/g, with integrals taken to vanish at A. The next page carries this through: there the pressure decays or relaxes exponentially, p = Ce^{−αx/g} + (g/α)(1 − e^{−αx/g}), and the jump terms at the junction E/F are added.
errors: Sign error in the series expansion. The coefficient of α^2 coming from αb^4v e^{−αr}∫e^{αr}ds/z^5 is −α^2 b^4 v r∫ds/z^5 + α^2 b^4 v∫r ds/z^5. The print has '+ααb^4vr∫ds/z^5'; it should be minus. All the other α^2 and α^3 terms check out.

Constant bookkeeping. If integrals vanish at the top, step (ii) gives a boundary term +b^4v/(4g^4) that is not written out; it is silently absorbed into C on this page. The next page restores it as 1/g^4 in '4∫e^{αr}dz/z^5 = 1/g^4 − e^{αr}/z^4 + ...'. So C here is not the same as the C later set equal to the atmospheric head l unless that shift is accounted for.

Notational clash. In §25, b denotes the tube length DF, while b^4 in the pressure formula is the earlier (orifice-related) velocity parameter. These are not the same quantity; the orifice is later called hh.

ideas.what: Linear first-order ODE for pressure along a pipe, solved by the integrating factor e^{α∫ds/z}, followed by integration by parts to remove the dx and dz quadratures
ideas.modern_name: integrating factor method / variation of constants
ideas.where_published: E260 itself; method standard in Euler's Institutiones calculi integralis (E342)

ideas.what: Expansion of the exact solution in powers of the small friction coefficient α up to third order
ideas.modern_name: regular perturbation expansion in a small parameter

ideas.what: Friction in pipe flow modelled as a force proportional to pressure divided by the tube's linear size, giving exponential pressure decay along a uniform pipe
ideas.modern_name: early hydraulic head-loss model (non-Darcy, Coulomb-type friction law)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E260); later velocity-based laws by Chézy, Prony, Darcy–Weisbach
ideas.where_published: E260, Novi Comm. Acad. Sci. Petrop. 6 (1756/57, publ. 1761); discussed by Truesdell in his introduction to Opera omnia II.12

ideas.what: Model problem: a constantly full vertical reservoir feeding an inclined cylindrical outlet pipe with an orifice

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine calculus: integration by parts and a power-series expansion inside a known memoir whose pressure-proportional friction hypothesis Truesdell already discussed. The only finding is a minor sign misprint in the α^2 term.
transcription_corrections: 'ficque' should read 'sicque', 'fiue' should read 'siue', and 'cafus/fpecialiores/poteft/fupremum/vafi/bafi/pertufus/conferuatur/fit/fupremo/euanefcant' use long s, i.e. s, not f.
Line 6 of the series: the print indeed reads '+ ααb^4vr∫ds/z^5'; the transcription is faithful, but mathematically the sign should be −.
In the last lines of the series the printed signs look like '+' (rendered as '-|-'); the transcription '+' is correct.
